M.A.S.K. for Essence20

Homebrew support for playing M.A.S.K. - the Mobile Armored Strike Kommand against V.E.N.O.M. - with the Essence20 system. Nothing here is code: it is compendium content built on the system's own homebrew features (game lines, vehicle Alt Modes, power gear), so you can copy how it's done for your own cartoon.

Setting up a world

  • Set the Game Line (Configure Settings) to M.A.S.K. - this module adds it. It plays on the G.I. Joe rules: agents take G.I. Joe Roles and Origins as well as the Mask Agent Role, and the Party is a Strike Team.
  • Turn on Alt Modes on Vehicles and Zords (Configure Settings). Every M.A.S.K. vehicle converts into its Strike Mode with that.
  • The M.A.S.K. compendiums sit in their own M.A.S.K. folder; picking a game line never switches a module's books off.

World settings

M.A.S.K. needs no house rules of its own. What used to be house rules is now part of the content:

  • The M.A.S.K. game line comes from this module's module.json (flags.essence20.gameLines): built on G.I. Joe, its compendiums in the M.A.S.K. folder. The Mask Agent Role names it. A GM can give it its own words for the book's (Configure Settings → Game Lines) - "Strike Mode" for "Alt Mode", say.
  • Bonded masks: each mask's own Bonded box (its Power Gear section). Untick it on a mask anyone may use.
  • Concealed weapons: a Strike-only weapon is an upgrade with Alt Mode only ticked (Power Gear) - in Civilian Mode its button isn't there at all.
  • Disguised vehicles: a rule on every Strike Mode - Edge on the vehicle's Deception and Infiltration Tests, when not:self:transformed.

Masks

A mask is a piece of gear with the system's Power Gear section filled in (the Details tab): Bonded ticked and Slot "mask". Wearing it is having it equipped. Masks also carry the flag flags.essence20-homebrew-starter.mask: true, which the guide's tables read.

  • Its power is a Use rule, usable a number of times per scene equal to the wearer's Speed: limit {per: scene, max: @essence.speed}.
  • The helmet - its protection - is an ordinary Defense rule.
  • Bonds: a mask nobody has worn bonds to the first agent who puts it on, and works - power and helmet - only for them. A mask taken from someone stays theirs until the GM presses Rebond on its sheet (after the lab work and downtime the story calls for - a Smarts (Technology) test is a good fit).
  • One at a time: putting a mask on takes off the one in the same slot.
  • Rules that care about masks use the slot: self:slotEquipped:mask (wearing a working mask), self:slotEquipped:mask:Spectrum (that one), self:crewSlotEquipped:mask:Spectrum (someone aboard a vehicle wears it).

Vehicles: Civilian and Strike Mode

Each M.A.S.K. vehicle is built as it looks on the road - its Civilian Mode. Its Strike Mode is an Alt Mode item (with Alt Modes on Vehicles and Zords on): the vehicle's Transform button converts it, and back. The Alt Mode holds what changes - its movement, its size, and its Toughness and Evasion. Each weapon system is its own upgrade; a Strike-only one has Alt Mode only ticked (Power Gear), so its Use button appears only in Strike Mode. Vehicles roll their weapons with their own Skill dice.

A vehicle's linked mask power - a crew member's mask firing through it - is a Use with the condition self:crewSlotEquipped:mask:<mask name>, once per scene. It appears only while someone aboard wears that mask (and it works for them).

Vehicles that carry another (the Rhino's ATV) keep its token hidden on the scene. Target it and press the carrier's Deploy: it appears just beside the carrier. Dock hides it again. The crew move across by dragging.

Defenses are the system's own: base 10 plus Strength (Toughness) or Speed (Evasion). A vehicle with no qualified driver moves at half speed - that is the system's rule too.

Origins, Perks and Features compendium has templates to drop on any vehicle and adjust: @UUID[Compendium.essence20-homebrew-starter.mask_options.Item.3PPNE2gDJoJ9Fvfa]{Concealed Weapon (template)}, @UUID[Compendium.essence20-homebrew-starter.mask_options.Item.9L1AyAIRru563SiE]{Linked Mask Power (template)}, @UUID[Compendium.essence20-homebrew-starter.mask_options.Item.X4kmerIdGq2fXrE1]{Strike Mode (template)}, @UUID[Compendium.essence20-homebrew-starter.mask_options.Item.ndCOaiYZSP7aWc7W]{Vehicle Bay (template)}.

Mask roster

Every mask in the M.A.S.K. Masks compendium. Powers are this module's own design - the toys only name each mask and what it does. Each works for its bonded agent a number of times per scene equal to their Speed, and every mask gives +1 Toughness to whoever wears it. New Blaster and New Torch were planned for the toy line but never sold.

Origins work like the book's: drop one on a character, pick the Essence to raise and a Skill from its list, and it sets starting Health and Ground Movement and grants its Origin Perk. Putting on a mask

The system doesn't charge an action for equipping gear, so this is a table rule: putting on or swapping a mask is the Draw Weapon action (a Move action). The Quick Change Perk makes it Free once per turn.

Agent roster

Every named agent of both sides, built with the system's Threat Builder (Field Guide rules) and ready to drop on a scene: NPC stat blocks, each wearing their signature mask with their other masks in their gear, carrying the M.A.S.K. Perks that suit them. Open one's sheet and use Check Against Threat Rules to see the build. Stats are our own homebrew.

  • Masks come bonded to their agent. Imported into a world, an agent rebonds its own masks automatically.
  • Vehicles: each agent's biography links theirs. Drag the agent onto the vehicle's crew to drive it - the linked mask powers then appear on the vehicle.
  • Threat Levels run from 4 for most agents to 8 for Matt Trakker and Miles Mayhem. For a party, the right Threat Level is its total levels / 4.
  • Players build their own agents as G.I. Joe characters with the M.A.S.K. Origins and Perks (the Agents page). These NPCs are allies, rivals and examples.

Running a campaign

Boulder Hill

@UUID[Compendium.essence20-homebrew-starter.mask_vehicles.Actor.7QyiP23m5sDqeLxg]{Boulder Hill} is the team's home: a country gas station that converts into a fortified headquarters (Strike Mode: +3 Toughness, rooftop lasers and a hillside cannon). Put it on the scene like any vehicle and add whoever is on duty to its crew. Its facilities are upgrades on it:

  • Command Center: Automatic: anyone crewing Boulder Hill (on duty in the base) has Edge on Alertness and Technology Tests.
  • Repair Bay: Use button: once per scene, the targeted vehicle regains 10 Health.
  • Hidden Hangar: Keep a stored vehicle's token hidden on the scene. Target it, then Deploy: it rolls out beside the base. Dock hides it again.
  • Mask Lab: Use button: posts the lab work to chat. Left to the table: the test and the downtime; the GM then presses Rebond on the mask's sheet.

The players' Party actor is still where the Requisition pool and Story Points live; Boulder Hill is the place.

The episode tools

Heists and races run on two GM tools the Essence20 system has for any show. Turn on Episode Tools: Mission Generator and Race Tracker under Configure Settings; the Mission Generator's button is then at the bottom of the Journal tab, and the Race and Chase Tracker's is in the Token controls.

V.E.N.O.M. heists

The cartoon's missions start with V.E.N.O.M. going after something valuable. Open the Mission Generator and pick M.A.S.K. Mission Tables: V.E.N.O.M. Heist. Roll draws from the six heist tables - @UUID[Compendium.essence20-homebrew-starter.mask_tables.RollTable.x4cVbUEmDaYubsC3]{Complication}, @UUID[Compendium.essence20-homebrew-starter.mask_tables.RollTable.KaxDppq2jXxiVvw7]{Cover}, @UUID[Compendium.essence20-homebrew-starter.mask_tables.RollTable.oUF7LxOx9i19S7eR]{Crew}, @UUID[Compendium.essence20-homebrew-starter.mask_tables.RollTable.uV1ND5eqUEiQuKhw]{Location}, @UUID[Compendium.essence20-homebrew-starter.mask_tables.RollTable.BNXyPe25sYWaBXAI]{Prize}, @UUID[Compendium.essence20-homebrew-starter.mask_tables.RollTable.0SGFDQqLMTok6cFX]{Scheme} - and you can reroll any one you don't like. Write Journal makes a journal entry with each draw (the agent leading the job links to their sheet; the Agent roster page lists their vehicles) and a four-step outline. Its title and outline are yours to change; the generator remembers them.

The racing season

Some missions are races - often with V.E.N.O.M. cheating to win a prize worth stealing.

  1. Set up. Roll or pick a course (@UUID[Compendium.essence20-homebrew-starter.mask_tables.RollTable.AygD95I04pREo9k6]{Course}, @UUID[Compendium.essence20-homebrew-starter.mask_tables.RollTable.nv33YeDLaD9H1RDJ]{Hazard}) - or pick M.A.S.K. Mission Tables: Racing Season in the Mission Generator for a write-up. The course's line gives the Driving DIF. A race is usually three laps. Open the Race and Chase Tracker, select the racers' tokens and Add Selected Tokens, and pick @UUID[Compendium.essence20-homebrew-starter.mask_tables.RollTable.nv33YeDLaD9H1RDJ]{Hazard} as its hazard table with "Roll a hazard when the leader starts a new lap" ticked.
  2. Each lap. Each driver makes a Driving test against the DIF. Everyone who succeeds completes the lap: + on their row. Degrees of Success settle who is ahead within a lap.
  3. Dirty tricks. Instead of driving flat out, a racer can attack: a vehicle weapon (in Strike Mode) or a mask power. A racer who attacks makes their Driving test with a Snag that lap.
  4. The finish. The first to the last lap wins; ties go to the higher Driving total. Post Standings any time; Reset clears every racer's laps. For a chase, set the tracker to Lead and count who's pulling away.

Secret identities

Agents with the Secret Identity Perk carry a Cover pool of 5 (the Agents page). Spend it when the story calls for it: an agent seen unmasking, a vehicle followed home, a heist complication. At 0, V.E.N.O.M. knows who they are.
